proof:
# A finite cap certificate for optimized unequal-endpoint selectors

Let d>=1. This concerns three positive fibers A,B,C at -1,0,1, with volumes
0<a=|A|<c=|C| and b=|B|. Assume (A+C)/2 is contained in B, and assume
the nonheavy inequalities c<a+b and b<a+c. It gives an exact finite
selection/cap mechanism. It does not assert the missing unconditional
three-fiber bound.

## 1. The moment body of the selectable endpoint mass

Let Sigma_a(C) consist of measures sigma<=1_C dx of mass a, and set

    M_a(C)={integral x d sigma: sigma in Sigma_a(C)},
    Y={ [b g_B+a g_A+m]/(b+2a): m in M_a(C)}.            (1)

Sigma_a(C) is weakly compact and convex: its mass and domination
constraints are closed on the compact set C. Its moment map is continuous,
so M_a(C) and Y are compact convex sets.

For every sigma in Sigma_a(C), the dominated-midpoint construction applies
to the two probability densities 1_A/a and sigma/a. They are both bounded
by 1/a; the Gaussian triangular-map proof does not require the second to
be an indicator. It gives eta<=1_B dx of mass a with mean
(a g_A+integral x d sigma)/(2a). Therefore y in (1) is the centroid of
1_B dx+2eta and is in B. For every ambient halfspace H containing (0,y),

 |A intersect H_-1|+|B intersect H_0|+|C intersect H_1|
   >= |B intersect H_0|+eta(H_0)
   >= (gamma_d/2)(b+2a).                               (2)

The last step includes vertical halfspaces as in the conditional
three-fiber theorem. Thus the ENTIRE convex selector body Y has the
guarantee (2), not merely a selected centroid.

For u!=0, the minimum of u.m over M_a(C) is achieved by the uniform
submeasure on an a-volume lower cap

    C_u=C intersect {u.x<=t_u},       |C_u|=a.           (3)

The threshold exists because the scalar projection law of volume on a
positive convex body is continuous and strictly increasing in its interior.
Its hyperplane boundaries have volume zero. To prove the minimizing
assertion, compare any admissible density with the indicator in (3):
their mass difference is zero, and the integral of (u.x-t_u) times their
difference is nonnegative. Equality forces the same indicator almost
everywhere. This also proves uniqueness of the minimizing moment for u!=0.

## 2. An exact finite certificate for strict failure over Y

Let mu be the unnormalized mixed volume on the three fibers, M=a+b+c.
Suppose a threshold tau satisfies

    max_(y in Y) inf_(H contains (0,y)) mu(H)<tau
                     < min(a+b,b+c).                  (4)

Then there exist y_* in Y, k<=d+1 closed ambient caps

    H_j={ (z,x): v_j z+u_j.x>=beta_j },
    u_j!=0,       mu(H_j)<tau,

and weights lambda_j>0 summing to one such that

    u_j.y_*=beta_j                 for every j,
    u=sum_j lambda_j u_j,
    u.(y-y_*)>=0                 for every y in Y.      (5)

If u!=0, the point y_* is generated by the actual uniform cap C_u in (3).
If u=0, the cap normals have a positive continuous-normal circuit and the
caps cover the whole continuous space at the median fiber.

Proof. Every point of Y has an ambient cap of mass less than tau. Its
continuous normal must be nonzero: a vertical cap containing the middle
fiber has mass at least min(a+b,b+c). Enlarge each chosen cap slightly so
its trace contains a neighborhood of the point while its mass stays below
tau. This is possible because a nonvertical boundary has zero volume in
each full-dimensional fiber, so cap mass is continuous under threshold
translations. Compactness gives a finite open cap cover of Y.

Apply finite-dimensional Helly to Y and the closed complements of these
open traces. At most d+1 sets have empty intersection. If Y is among them,
at most d caps are needed; otherwise at most d+1 caps already cover the
whole space. In either case keep at most d+1 caps covering Y by their open
traces, and write their margins as m_j(y)=u_j.y-beta_j.

The continuous convex function max_j m_j has on Y an attained positive
minimum t. Finite convex minimax gives weights lambda_j>=0, sum one, with

    min_(y in Y) sum_j lambda_j m_j(y)=t.

Here is a direct separation proof: the image {(m_1(y),...,m_k(y)):y in Y}
is compact convex and disjoint from the open box whose coordinates are
all below t. A separating vector has nonnegative coordinates, can be
normalized to sum one, and has minimum value t. At any primal minimizer
y_*, all m_j(y_*)<=t, so every positive lambda_j has m_j(y_*)=t.

Discard zero weights and increase the remaining thresholds by t. The
resulting caps pass through y_*, have no larger masses, and satisfy (5).
Indeed the weighted new margin is u.(y-y_*), whose minimum on Y is zero.
For u!=0, minimizing u.y in (1) selects exactly (3), proving the stated
description of y_*. This proves the certificate.

Conversely, any configuration satisfying (5) has its closed cap traces
covering Y: their weighted margins are nonnegative there, so at least one
individual margin is nonnegative. If all cap masses are below tau, every
point of Y has depth below tau. Thus this is an exact finite certificate
for strict failure, with the cap-selector conclusion when u!=0.

## 3. Exact unused-endpoint order in the aggregate cap normal

In the nonzero-u case put sigma=1_(C_u) dx and xi=1_C dx-sigma, whose
mass is delta=c-a. The selected measure lies below the threshold t_u and
the unused measure above it. Consequently, for EVERY real s,

    xi{u.x>=s}/delta >= sigma{u.x>=s}/a.                (6)

For s<=t_u the left side is one, and for s>t_u the right side is zero.
Boundary hyperplanes have zero volume. In particular their scalar means
satisfy

    (1/delta)integral u.x dxi
       >= (1/a)integral u.x d sigma.                   (7)

The same first-moment order holds for the weighted ambient margin on the
larger endpoint, since its extra constant is common:

 (1/delta)integral sum_j lambda_j(v_j+u_j.x-beta_j) dxi
   >=(1/a)integral sum_j lambda_j(v_j+u_j.x-beta_j) d sigma. (8)

The corresponding full selected triple has weighted first-margin integral
zero at the through-y_* certificate, because y_* is its continuous
centroid and the selected endpoint masses are equal. Before the common
threshold shift in the proof, this integral was (b+2a)t>0.

Equation (6) is a simultaneous statement for all thresholds of the ONE
averaged normal u. It does not claim stochastic domination separately in
the normals u_j. Passing from this aggregate order, the strict small cap
masses, and the domination/coupling information to the required additional
gamma_d(c-a)/2 budget is the remaining step.

## 4. Exact decomposition of the missing cap budget

For the selected sigma, let pi be any dominated-midpoint coupling of the
mass-a endpoint measures 1_A dx and sigma, and let eta=T#pi. For an
ambient cap H define its nonnegative pairing slack

 P_H=integral [1_H(-1,x)+1_H(1,x')-1_H(0,(x+x')/2)] d pi.

The endpoint indicator inequality proves P_H>=0, including closed-boundary
cases. There is the exact identity

    mu(H)=|B intersect H_0|+eta(H_0)+xi(H_1)+P_H.        (9)

At every containing cap, the first two terms have sandwich lower bound
gamma_d(b+2a)/2. In particular, if the finite certificate uses the desired
threshold tau=gamma_d(a+b+c)/2, it satisfies

 sum_j lambda_j { xi((H_j)_1)+P_(H_j)
       +|B intersect (H_j)_0|+eta((H_j)_0)
                           -gamma_d(b+2a)/2 }
      < gamma_d(c-a)/2.                               (10)

Every summand inside braces is nonnegative. Equations (5), (6), (8),
and (10) constitute a finite subset-selection/endcap-gain system with
actual ambient caps and an actual dominated coupling. They neither discard
the pairing slack nor replace the individual cap indicators by their
averaged affine margin. That final passage is exactly what is not yet
proved.
